data.narrative:
Planted Solar, a Series A climate and energy company founded by Eric Brown, has raised $32M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (Lonza, ticker LNZA) across the Climate & Energy sector, including companies such as Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

The stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach. Using the $32M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression to the next financing stage yields an implied valuation of $64M. A peer-median approach could not be reliably applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within a narrow valuation tier—while 9 same-sector peers exist, none met the threshold of ≥3 datapoints across filtered subsets. Deploying an all-sector median would introduce material bias.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $54M to $74M, centered on a $64M median. This range reflects ±15% variance around the stage-progression estimate to account for company-specific execution risk, market timing, and the acknowledged thinness of the direct peer set. The principal uncertainty remains the limited availability of proximate private comparables at Series A in this subsector, which constrains confidence in cross-sectional validation. Revenue, profitability, or technology-stage data would materially narrow this range.
